10. Which of the following mixtures can be separated by the process of mag-
netic separation?
(a) Chalk powder + sand (b) Iron + sand
(c) Sulphur + calcium (d) Common salt + sand

11. In which among the following cases is adhesive force predominant over
cohesive force?
(a) Water in capillary tube.
(b) Mercury in capillary tube.
(c) Water in a test tube in which the inner wall is coated with wax.
(d) Water on leaves of aquatic plants.

12. Which of the following gaseous mixtures can be separated by using KOH as
a solvent?
(a) $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{SO}_2$ (b) $\mathrm{N}_2$ and $\mathrm{NH}_3$
(c) $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ (d) $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{N}_2$

13. Four gases A, B, C, and D have critical temperatures $32^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $-118^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $31.1^\circ\mathrm{C}$,
and $-140^\circ\mathrm{C}$, respectively. Arrange them in the increasing order of ease of
liquefaction of the gases.
(a) $\mathrm{D} < \mathrm{B} < \mathrm{C} < \mathrm{A}$ (b) $\mathrm{A} > \mathrm{B} > \mathrm{D} > \mathrm{C}$
(c) $\mathrm{C} < \mathrm{D} < \mathrm{B} < \mathrm{A}$ (d) $\mathrm{A} < \mathrm{C} < \mathrm{B} < \mathrm{D}$

14. An increase in pressure increases the melting point. This statement is true
for ______.
(a) ice and brass (b) silver and gold
(c) brass and gold (d) ice and silver

15. Which among the following disappears with time without heating?
(a) Ammonium chloride (b) Naphthalene
(c) Sodium chloride (d) Sulphur
